Recent work supports retaining several interests and learning intent boundaries. S2-CAR (2026 preprint) directly addresses this: a context-aware temporal point process tracks latent intent energy, triggers segmentation through energy decay, and aggregates coherent segments into an adaptive number of interest representations. It challenges both homogeneous history pooling and fixed time-gap segmentation; reported backbone integration makes segmentation a useful architectural direction, although single-GPU cost here remains unverified. [S2-CAR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25415)

Preserving multiple vectors also requires preventing collapse. KDD 2024’s Disentangled Multi-interest Representation Learning partitions items using global co-purchase likelihood, aligning partition learning with interest modeling through sampled graph contrastive optimization. This supplies behavioral supervision for distinct interests without requiring pretrained text representations. For persistent versus local preferences, LS4SRec (2025) uses separate long- and short-term encoders plus a global interaction graph; its additional graph machinery would require a budget check. [Disentangled multi-interest learning](https://doi.org/10.1145/3637528.3671800), [LS4SRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723173)

Practical synthesis for this budget—an experimental adaptation, not a published performance claim: retain SASRec’s recent-state vector, add 2–4 attention-pooled history interests, and learn candidate-dependent gating between persistent interests and current intent. Compare fixed recent windows against causal boundaries derived from timestamp gaps and learned item-embedding changes; use a small interest-separation penalty and monitor collapse. Train entirely from public histories; optional title/description TF-IDF can provide an additional similarity signal. Validate each addition using the common macro HR@10. The cited studies motivate these components but do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness protocol.
